note.question: How should an e-commerce seller set scarce inventory when consumers value rarity and strategically sort across simultaneous auctions?
note.overview: Local bidders strategically choose between two simultaneous uniform-price auctions under incomplete information, and the paper estimates a symmetric Bayesian Nash cutoff equilibrium.

components.label: Symmetric Bayesian Nash cutoff-entry equilibrium
components.explanation: The model's equilibrium concept is Symmetric Bayesian Nash cutoff-entry equilibrium. Proposition 1, printed p. 3556 (PDF p. 7), proves existence of a symmetric cutoff equilibrium and payoff equivalence of pure-strategy equilibria. Multiple cutoffs are theoretically possible, while the estimation routine numerically finds a unique equilibrium.

components.label: Model sequence and system structure
components.explanation: The seller commits inventory and reserve prices for simultaneous multiunit uniform-price auctions. Bidders observe these terms and private values; global bidders enter any auction above reserve, while local bidders strategically choose one auction. Bids then determine uniform clearing prices. Global bidders generate cross-auction demand without an exclusivity constraint.
